steps.title: Cabernet Sauvignon
steps.body: Cabernet Sauvignon is Maipo's signature: ripe blackcurrant and cherry, often with a distinctive mint or eucalyptus note, firm but ripe tannins and fresh acidity. Many Chilean icon wines, like Almaviva, a Concha y Toro and Mouton Rothschild partnership, and Don Melchor, are Maipo Cabernets.

steps.title: Carmenère
steps.body: Carmenère, brought from Bordeaux in the 19th century, was mixed with Merlot for over a century. In 1994, French ampelographer Jean-Michel Boursiquot identified it. It needs a long, warm season; in Maipo it gives dark fruit, spice and soft tannins, with a green pepper note if unripe. Merlot, Syrah and Cabernet Franc are also grown.
The mint note in Maipo Cabernet is linked by some to eucalyptus trees nearby and by others to the grape's own compounds.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Cabernet Sauvignon is Maipo's signature, often minty
Icons like Almaviva and Don Melchor are Maipo Cabernets
